I'm extremely disappointed with the Euro Kids Suyog Nagar branch. Despite the brand's reputation, this school falls short in every aspect. There's a lack of management, and the education system is subpar. The Euro Kids app often doesn't work or update on time, leaving parents uninformed.

My child was shown TV continuously, supposedly to keep them engaged, but it felt like a lack of effort from the teachers. Festivals were celebrated without any enthusiasm or interest. The constant change of teachers meant my child didn't get stability or quality education. At times, one teacher handled all the kids, which is unacceptable.

The class activity will be done by teachers itself just to show that your child is doing it but in reality they just complete the worksheet on thier own. Sometimes they dont even know which child has which quality or ability to explore.

The school's approach to education is superficial, and it seems like they're just going through the motions. Class activities are often done by teachers alone, with students merely filling out worksheets without understanding the concepts.

The teachers seem disinterested in recognizing individual students' abilities or talents. When questioned about specific issues, the school's responses are often dismissive and dishonest. They claim to be doing their best, but it's clear they're not putting in much effort.

The school's communication is also poor. Group activity photos are often blurry, and getting updates or photos of your child can be a struggle. You may have to follow up multiple times, and even then, you might not receive any updates.

The teachers appear to be unenthusiastic about teaching, and your child is unlikely to learn even the basics in this school. I would not recommend Euro Kids Suyog Nagar to anyone.

The school lacks space, which hinders a child's growth. I regret enrolling my child here and would advise others to avoid this branch at all costs. It's a waste of money, and the experience has been terrible

featured_reviews.review_text:
If there was an option to give zero stars, I would.

Today was the third day my children attended this daycare, and I am extremely disappointed by what I witnessed. My two toddlers of the same age were attending the settling session, accompanied by our nanny. At the time of the incident, one child was being comforted by the nanny as they were upset and crying. Of the three staff members present (two teachers and one support staff member), two were engaged with other children, leaving only one staff member in the immediate vicinity of my children.

What concerned me was that instead of actively supervising both children, the staff member nearby appeared focused on giving toys briefly and taking photographs on her phone of the child who was with the nanny. Meanwhile, my other child was moving around the room without adequate supervision.

The most serious issue was that the classroom door had been left unsecured. My child was able to open the door, walk outside, and reach a staircase where a fall occurred, resulting in injury and distress. What was even more alarming was that no staff member immediately attended to the crying child. As a parent present on the premises, I had to step in myself.

When the incident was raised, staff members appeared unsure about how the door had been left open. Rather than acknowledging the lapse in supervision and safety, blame was shifted onto our nanny, despite the fact that she was occupied attending to the other child who was distressed at the time.

A daycare's primary responsibility is to provide a safe, secure, and supervised environment for children.
